summary: The proposal asked whether the other at-most-one ClassFile attributes deserve the rule BootstrapMethods got, and guessed the answer might be no for the ones nothing reads. Measured against OpenJDK 26.0.1 one attribute at a time, the answer is yes for five of them — and the proposal's stated cost, 'rejecting more files that load today', is false: a real JVM already refuses every one of those files. The interesting part is the two it does not refuse, which is why this is a version-gated table rather than a rule over every single-valued attribute.
changes: classfile/src/validation.rs: at_most_one_bootstrap_methods_attribute -> at_most_one_of_each_single_class_attribute, a version-gated table over SourceFile, InnerClasses, SourceDebugExtension, BootstrapMethods, NestHost, NestMembers

classfile/src/attribute.rs: one parse arm for SourceDebugExtension, which makes an existing but unreachable enum variant live. Without it a duplicate lands in Unknown, where it is indistinguishable from two attributes we do not recognise.
test-data/src/attr/make_attr_fixtures.py: new generator for duplicate-attribute fixtures, carrying the measurement in its docstring
test-data/attr/: 7 fixtures — 5 that must be rejected, 2 controls that must keep loading
tests/test_class_format.rs: test_a_class_declaring_a_single_valued_attribute_twice_is_malformed, a table with a `loads` column
test-data/class-file-versions.txt: +7 rows for the new fixtures (AGENTS.md requires the table move with the fixture)
verification: ORACLE, measured one attribute at a time with OpenJDK 26.0.1 via Class.forName rather than the launcher (whose 'no main method' message hides the real cause): duplicated SourceFile / InnerClasses / SourceDebugExtension / BootstrapMethods at major 52 -> ClassFormatError: Multiple <name> attributes; duplicated NestHost / NestMembers at major 55 -> same

CONTROL 1 — duplicated NestHost at major 52 LOADS. The attribute is not defined before 55, so it is ignored (JVMS 4.7.1) and there is nothing to duplicate. A rule without a version gate would reject a file every JVM accepts.

CONTROL 2 — duplicated Synthetic at major 52 LOADS, though JVMS 4.7.8 marks it at-most-one. The spec and HotSpot disagree; we follow the JVM. Nothing here reads the attribute either, so there is no arbitrary choice to make observable.
so the proposal's tradeoff premise is measurably false for the five: those files do not 'load today' on a real JVM — our accepting them was the deviation

criterion re-derived from the existing check's own comment (a duplicate makes an arbitrary choice observable downstream) and then measured: the only class-level attribute read with a first-wins selector is BootstrapMethods (validation.rs find_map and jvm-bytecode/src/string_concat.rs resolve_bootstrap_methods find_map). Consumers outside attribute.rs for SourceFile / InnerClasses / SourceDebugExtension / NestHost / NestMembers / Synthetic: zero. So the downstream-observability argument alone would have stopped at 'no' — the JVM oracle is what moved it.
MUTATION M1, delete the version gate: control DuplicateNestHostOldMajor turns red (we would reject what the JVM loads)
MUTATION M2, add Synthetic to the table: control DuplicateSynthetic turns red
MUTATION M3, remove the SourceFile row: that fixture alone stops being rejected, red
MUTATION M4, revert the call site to the BootstrapMethods-only form: the five turn red
generator is idempotent: a second run leaves the fixture bytes unchanged
cargo test --all and the DoD commands: see the round's REPORT.md entry
issues: Product behaviour changes: a class carrying two of those five attributes now fails to load where it used to run. That is the point, and every such file is one OpenJDK also refuses — but it is a behaviour change, not a no-op.
The table is a written-down list, not derived. An attribute added to AttributeInfo tomorrow is not covered until someone adds a row, and nothing flags that.
Synthetic is excluded on one JVM's behaviour. If HotSpot tightened, or another JVM already rejects it, our control fixture would be pinning the wrong answer.

attribute.rs was touched even though the proposal's target is validation.rs. One arm, and it was the minimum to cover an attribute the JVM rejects — but it is outside the named file and is reported as such.
